title: 2003 AMC 10B Problem 21
statement: A bag contains two red beads and two green beads. You reach into the bag and pull out a bead, replacing it with a red bead regardless of the color you pulled out. What is the probability that all beads in the bag are red after three such replacements?

solutions.text:
The bag always holds \(4\) beads. All are red at the end precisely when both greens are drawn.

Drawing green then green has probability \(\dfrac24 \cdot \dfrac14 = \dfrac18.\) Green, red, green has probability \(\dfrac24 \cdot \dfrac34 \cdot \dfrac14 = \dfrac{3}{32}.\) Red, green, green has probability \(\dfrac24 \cdot \dfrac24 \cdot \dfrac14 = \dfrac{1}{16}.\)

The total is \[\dfrac18 + \dfrac{3}{32} + \dfrac{1}{16} = \dfrac{9}{32}.\]

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: All beads are red exactly when both green beads are drawn during the three draws
Add the probabilities of the draw sequences GG, GRG, and RGG, tracking how the counts change
